section_summary: This section chiefly records the 1947 dispute over a second Japanese Antarctic whaling expedition. British and Australian officials objected to its authorization, while U.S. and occupation authorities defended it on food, economic and procedural grounds. The section also includes reports on the previous expedition, arrangements to ship whale oil from Japan to Germany, and several adjacent records on other subjects.

subfiles.title: Conversation with Dr. Evatt regarding Japanese whaling, Manus Island, and international finance
subfiles.doc_type: Embassy despatch with memorandum and newspaper clipping
subfiles.about: Reports Evatt’s objections to Japanese whaling and his complaints about Manus Island and an international financial directorship.
subfiles.summary: The covering despatch reports a June 24 conversation in which Evatt objected to another Japanese whaling expedition, questioned U.S. handling of Manus Island equipment and bases, and discussed an Australian directorship of the International Bank and Monetary Fund. An enclosed conversation memorandum gives Butler’s account. A Sydney Morning Herald editorial criticizes U.S. action on whaling and Angaur phosphate without Allied consultation.

subfiles.title: Second Japanese Antarctic whaling expedition
subfiles.about: Lovett suggests a conditional response to Australia’s offer to operate a whaling unit.
subfiles.summary: Lovett proposes accepting Australian operation only if Australia supplies the whale oil and meat Japan would otherwise obtain.

subfiles.title: Note for General Hilldring
subfiles.about: Routes a note marked by the Secretary for General Hilldring.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary has marked an attached note for Hilldring; Reams requests necessary action.

subfiles.title: Appointment with Mr. Balfour
subfiles.about: Prepares Lovett for a British Embassy meeting on the second Japanese whaling expedition.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum traces SCAP’s request, British and Dominion objections, U.S. consultations, and authorization of the expedition. It recommends emphasizing Japan’s food needs, the cost to the United States, and the time available for protests.

subfiles.title: Conversation with Sir John Balfour on Japanese whaling
subfiles.about: Records British objections and Lovett’s defense of the whaling authorization.
subfiles.summary: Balfour presents a British protest alleging inadequate consultation and seeking Far Eastern Commission review. Lovett explains the U.S. procedural position and argues that Japanese whale meat and oil reduce occupation costs. The participants discuss British factory ships, the international catch limit, and alternative supply arrangements.

subfiles.title: Record copy replacement for Tokyo despatch 1146
subfiles.about: Designates a copy of Tokyo despatch 1146 as the record copy.
subfiles.summary: Replaces the unreturned original action copy of Tokyo despatch 1146.

subfiles.title: House of Commons questions on Japanese whaling
subfiles.about: Transmits British parliamentary questions and an answer concerning the second Japanese Antarctic expedition.
subfiles.summary: Members question U.S. authority and consultation; Mayhew says the British Ambassador will reopen the matter with Washington.

subfiles.title: Authorization of Japanese whaling operations in the Antarctic, 1947–1948
subfiles.about: Forwards SCAP instructions authorizing Japanese Antarctic whaling.
subfiles.summary: Forwards copies of SCAPIN 1737 and a memorandum delivered to the Japanese Government.

subfiles.title: British note protesting the second Japanese whaling expedition
subfiles.about: Requests reconsideration and Far Eastern Commission review of the whaling decision.
subfiles.summary: Britain says U.S. authorization breached its prior assurance of consultation and disregarded pending Far Eastern Commission work. It asks that MacArthur’s instructions be countermanded and Australian alternatives examined.

subfiles.title: U.S. response to British notes on whaling consultation
subfiles.about: Defends U.S. consultation and refuses to cancel the second expedition.
subfiles.summary: The Department recounts discussions and exchanges from April through June and maintains that interested governments had ample opportunity to state their views. It acknowledges confusion over promised Far Eastern Commission fishing and whaling papers. It says the Australian proposal would forgo foreign exchange and offers no sufficient security reason to abandon the expedition. The U.S. position is final.

subfiles.title: Australian government press statement on Japanese whaling
subfiles.about: Transmits Australia’s statement describing support for its position in the Far Eastern Commission.
subfiles.summary: The statement reports Allied support against unilateral U.S. authorization and quotes Evatt’s objections to Japanese whaling near Antarctic territories.

subfiles.title: Conversation with Australian Ambassador Makin
subfiles.doc_type: Memorandum of conversation with attached statement
subfiles.about: Records Makin’s appeal for reconsideration of the second expedition.
subfiles.summary: Makin reads a statement offering Australian operation of a whaling expedition and arguing that Japanese vessels near Australia pose a security risk. The Secretary promises to consider the points without giving an immediate answer.

subfiles.title: SCAP views on Australian objections to whaling
subfiles.to: War Department and Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Urges the United States to maintain authorization despite Australian protests.
subfiles.summary: SCAP argues that Australian operation would be impractical, less efficient, and inconsistent with occupation authority. The telegram disputes Australian security concerns and says reversal would harm Japanese food supplies, morale, and U.S. standing in the Far East. It invokes the Potsdam Declaration and other policy principles supporting Japan’s access to resources.

subfiles.title: Correction to Angaur Island press release
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Corrects wording in a Department press release on the Angaur phosphate industry.
subfiles.summary: Supplies corrected language on Australian concern about Japanese laborers and changes one word in the release.

subfiles.title: Angaur Island phosphate industry
subfiles.about: Explains SCAP supervision of Japanese work on Angaur’s phosphate industry.
subfiles.summary: Marshall says SCAP will supervise the project and return Japanese workers home after completion.

subfiles.title: Rejection of Australian proposal to operate a Japanese whaling unit
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Informs SCAP that Australia’s proposed operation of a whaling unit was rejected.
subfiles.summary: Quotes the U.S. reply citing low security risk and Japan’s need for a self-supporting economy.

subfiles.title: Draft telegram to SCAP on Australian whaling proposal
subfiles.about: Drafts the message rejecting Australian operation of a Japanese whaling unit.
subfiles.summary: Two draft versions quote the proposed U.S. explanation: the expedition presents no apparent security risk and supports Japan’s economy.

subfiles.title: McCoy–Makin exchange at the Far Eastern Commission
subfiles.about: Reports an argument over timing a vote on the Japanese whaling paper.
subfiles.summary: McCoy and Makin dispute whether U.S. requests for delay amount to deliberate procrastination.

subfiles.title: Australian observer’s report on the Hashidate Maru
subfiles.about: Forwards an Australian observer’s report on the 1946–47 Japanese whaling expedition.
subfiles.summary: Transmits a report on the mother ship and accompanying chasers.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Australian whaling report
subfiles.about: Acknowledges receipt of the Australian observer’s report.
subfiles.summary: Thanks the Ambassador for making the Hashidate Maru report available.

subfiles.title: Record copy replacement for Tokyo despatch 1188
subfiles.about: Designates a replacement record copy of Tokyo despatch 1188.
subfiles.summary: Replaces the unreturned original action copy of despatch 1188.

subfiles.title: Australian observer’s report concerning 1946–47 Japanese whaling
subfiles.about: Forwards the Australian report and SCAP’s detailed criticism of its conclusions.
subfiles.summary: SCAP’s Natural Resources Section disputes the observer’s estimates of discarded bones and lost oil, argues that the expedition made effective use of whale products, and challenges claims that Australians could immediately operate a comparably efficient expedition.

subfiles.title: Norwegian inspector for the next Antarctic whaling expedition
subfiles.about: Welcomes Norway’s proposed inspector on the 1947–48 expedition.
subfiles.summary: Says SCAP will be informed so assignment details can be arranged in Tokyo.

subfiles.title: Whale oil transport from Japan to Germany
subfiles.about: Urges use of a Japanese whaling tanker to ship whale oil to Germany.
subfiles.summary: Donald says 7,100 tons of oil are urgently needed in Germany and that no suitable alternative tanker is readily available. He argues that using the American Coxcomb Hill would be costly, slow, and risk contamination.

subfiles.title: Status of whale oil shipping discussions
subfiles.about: Reports discussions with Britain about shipping whale oil to Germany.
subfiles.summary: Clarifies that State sought British consultation and suggests using cargo liner deep tanks.

subfiles.title: Reply to Dudley B. Donald
subfiles.about: Acknowledges Donald’s concerns about the whale oil shipment.
subfiles.summary: Lovett says he understands the problem and hopes a satisfactory solution will be found.

subfiles.title: Newmont mining concession in Siam
subfiles.doc_type: Departmental transmittal with business letter and proposed contract
subfiles.about: Forwards correspondence and draft terms for a mining concession on Koh Phangan.
subfiles.summary: The Department requests updates on Newmont’s negotiations. Enclosures include Schneider’s letter, Anaconda’s advice to Miller, and a draft mining lease covering prospecting, royalties, taxes, exports, personnel, currency exchange, and withdrawal rights.

subfiles.title: British Foreign Office position on Japanese whaling
subfiles.about: Reports British efforts to keep Australia and New Zealand from forcing a whaling vote.
subfiles.summary: MacDermot says Britain still opposes Japanese whaling but prefers to avoid a U.S.–British split over a Far Eastern Commission veto. He suggests leaving the issue for the peace conference.

subfiles.title: British assessment that the whaling dispute is subsiding
subfiles.about: Reports Commonwealth responses to Britain’s suggestion to drop the dispute.
subfiles.summary: MacDermot says New Zealand agreed and Australia reluctantly accepted; he expects little further diplomatic activity.

subfiles.title: U.S. assurances regarding future Japanese whaling expeditions
subfiles.about: Answers British requests for whaling safeguards and future consultation.
subfiles.summary: The United States promises supervision, Allied observers, and international allocation of whale oil. It declines to require Far Eastern Commission concurrence for every future expedition, while promising to seek interested governments’ views.

subfiles.title: Telephone conversation about Herrington’s fisheries letter
subfiles.about: Asks Deason to seek clarification of Herrington’s Japanese fishing proposals.
subfiles.summary: Deason agrees to ask about fishing areas and limiting fleet expansion in his personal reply.

subfiles.title: Herrington letter on Japanese fishing policy
subfiles.about: Lists concerns and proposals concerning Japanese fishing.
subfiles.summary: The surviving text asks about supplies, fleet limits, fishing rights, industry monopolies, and better statistics.

subfiles.title: British request for assurances on Japanese Antarctic whaling
subfiles.about: Requests limits and safeguards for present and future Japanese expeditions.
subfiles.summary: Britain disputes the U.S. account of prior consultation and asks for Far Eastern Commission concurrence on future expeditions, enforcement of whaling rules with Allied observers, and international allocation of whale oil.

subfiles.title: Whale oil shipments from Japan to Germany
subfiles.about: Identifies officials handling the proposed whale oil shipment.
subfiles.summary: Lists contacts and notes the urgency of finding cargo liner space before using a Japanese tanker.

subfiles.title: British applications to buy C-1 MAV-1 ships
subfiles.about: Reports a British Shipping Attaché’s call about ship purchase applications.
subfiles.summary: Cross seeks help with delayed British applications for three ships; Clancy will check Maritime Commission action.

subfiles.title: Approval to inform the British
subfiles.about: Conveys Colonel Harris’s approval for Britain to proceed.
subfiles.summary: Requests that Powell tell Cross the British can go ahead.

subfiles.title: Routing annotation
subfiles.about: Contains a partly illegible routing instruction.
subfiles.summary: A brief note addresses Powell; its substantive instruction is illegible.

subfiles.title: British arrangements for carrying whale oil to Germany
subfiles.about: Offers British cargo liner capacity for the whale oil shipment.
subfiles.summary: Cross says British lines can carry about 3,500 tons by November and the remainder by February 1948.

subfiles.title: Fragment of Donald’s whale oil transport letter
subfiles.about: Preserves the closing lines of a copy of Donald’s shipment letter.
subfiles.summary: The fragment repeats Donald’s call for prompt action on whale oil transport.
